lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.title: Performance task build: checking and interpreting

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: Set up the first two carefully; the rest of the build depends on them.

items.prompt: System: y = -2x - 14 and y = 3x + 26. Does the point (-7, 1) satisfy both equations, fail one, or fail both?
Plan A charges a $113 flat fee plus $4 per month. Plan B charges a $47 flat fee plus $10 per month. The solution to the system is (11, 157). What does the y-coordinate of the solution represent?
choices: The number of months after which the two plans cost the same.
The shared cost, in dollars, when the two plans are equal.
The difference in cost between the two plans.
The rate Plan B charges per month.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: System: y = x + 3 and y = -4x + 3. Which point (x, y) satisfies both equations?
Solve the system: y = 8x + 16 and y = -8x - 16. What is the intersection point (x, y)?
Relationship A: x: 4, 5, 6, 7 y: 15, 21, 27, 33. Relationship B: x: 4, 5, 6, 7 y: 15, 23, 31, 39. At which x-value do the two relationships have the same y-value?
Solve the system: y = 6x - 2 and y = 5x + 1. In which quadrant does the intersection point lie, or does it lie on an axis?

Solve the system:
y = -6x + 49
8x - 6y = 146
Use substitution to find the solution (x, y).

Solve the system:
4x + 9y = 150
-9x - 9y = -180
Use elimination to find the solution (x, y).

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Carry the build to a result and state the check that would catch an error in it.

items.prompt: Classify the system: y = -7x - 23 and y = -7x + 9. Does it have one solution, no solution, or infinitely many solutions?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: The reference equation is y = x + 22. Which of these equations, paired with the reference, would give the system no solution?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
